subject: Renewal proposal: convert retainer to committed throughput + temporary price hold
messages:

Subject: Renewal proposal: convert retainer to committed throughput + temporary price hold

Hi Liam —

Thanks again for the productive renewal call last week. Per our discussion, attached is a short amendment draft and a pricing matrix that converts your current monthly retainer into a 12-month committed throughput (measured in token-hours) for Core Inference and Embeddings. Key points in the draft: 

- 12-month committed volume equivalent to ~1.2x your trailing 12 month usage (smooths spikes)
- A 3-month temporary price hold on current unit pricing for any usage within the committed quantity
- A one-time onboarding credit to offset migration costs (see worksheet)
- Quarterly true-up with step-up option if consumption exceeds the committed tier

Two asks from your side that I noted: confirmation on the committed baseline and whether you want a phased uplift (2 quarters) vs. an all-in conversion day 1. I included a flexible table so we can toggle those options. 

If you want to walk through the matrix, I can run a short 20-minute call tomorrow. Otherwise, happy to accept markups to the attached PDF and return a final for signature.

Thanks,
Hannah

Subject: Re: Renewal proposal: convert retainer to committed throughput + temporary price hold

Thanks Hannah —

Appreciate the clear options. A couple of quick clarifications from our side: 

1) The committed baseline looks reasonable but can we make it a 10% uplift instead of 20%? The product team is confident the mothership rollout will add predictable traffic but we want to avoid overcommitting in Q1.

2) Sofia asked if the price hold can be extended to 6 months (instead of 3) for the first year to help us stabilize cost while we complete an infra optimization.

3) On onboarding credit — can that be applied as an invoice credit rather than an up-front rebate? That helps with our accounting treatment.

If those three tweaks are feasible, we should be able to sign quickly. We can also accept e-sign if you send a link.

— Liam

Ben / Monica — forwarding Liam's reply. Two asks: reduce the uplift to 10% baseline and extend the price hold to 6 months. Also they prefer the onboarding credit as an invoice credit.

Background: ClearPath is a mid-enterprise account with steady growth and a big product launch expected in Q4. They've been on a retainer with a lot of monthly variability; converting to a commit reduces our operational uncertainty and makes routing/bursting simpler. The requested changes would modestly reduce our near-term ARR but should avoid churn risk and make expansion more likely.

Proposal options for approval: 
- Option A (standard): Accept 10% uplift baseline, 6-month price hold, onboarding credit applied as invoice credit — give a one-time 7.5% credit (applied to first invoice after effective date). No other concessions.
- Option B (conservative): Same as A but reduce onboarding credit to a fixed $10k credit instead of percent.
- Option C (stretch): Keep 12-month 20% uplift but extend price hold to 6 months and offer a 10% first-year discount (higher cost to us).

Thoughts? If you OK Option A, I'll update the amendment and route a DocuSign link. I flagged this as time-sensitive — they want to close before month-end to align with budgeting.

Thanks,
Hannah

Hannah / Monica —

Option A is acceptable. Approve the 10% uplift baseline and a 6-month temporary price hold. For the onboarding credit, approve a one-time 7.5% credit applied against the first post-effective invoice (cap at $25k). Rationale: preserves predictable committed ARR while addressing ClearPath's accounting ask and reducing near-term friction.

Hannah — please update the amendment with those parameters and send for signature. Loop me if they ask for anything materially larger (>$25k) or request multi-year deep discounts.
